To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ODFs of hcp dysprosium, erbium, and their respective fluoride compounds can be accurately determined by Rietveld texture refinement using either GSAS or MAUD.

1) The GSAS Rietveld code is capable of determining the orientation distribution function (ODF) of a textured sample with a strong neutron absorber, and 2) The MAUD Rietvelt code can determine the atomic coordinates and the ODF of a textured sample that is a strong neutron absorbers.

(1) the GSAS and the MAUD Rietvel analysis packages are able to analyze data from highly absorbing samples, (2) the ODFs obtained from the two analysis packages are qualita- tively similar, and (3) the atomic positions are not affected by absorption.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of neutron absorption on Rietveld refinement and texture analysis.
the effects of absorption on texture refinement and structural parameters for highly absorbing samples.
the development and application of Rietveld texture and structural parameter refinements of strongly absorbing materials using neutron diffraction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MAUD method is not suitable for analysis of strongly absorbing materials.
for highly absorbing materials, Rietveld refinement is possible, and that the MAUD and GSAS packages can both be used for texture analysis.
the GSAS and the MAUD Rietveild codes give similar results when analyzing neutron powder data of strongly absorbing samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
strong absorption does not have a large impact on texture or structural refinement, and that the two analysis packages used here produce similar results.
Rietveld refinement for texture analysis of highly absorbing samples can be done with the proper care, but it requires more attention than for non-absorbing samples.
the MAUD method for texture analysis is more robust for highly absorbing materials than the GSAS method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
absorption is not an issue for texture analysis by Rietveld methods.
strong absorption for thermal neutron scattering does not affect Rietveld refinement of atomic positions.
strong absorption can be accounted for and does not significantly affect the refinement of structural parameters or texture.
